Legal

Privacy Policy

Quantica Education, Inc.  ·  Effective July 1, 2026  ·  Last updated August 9, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Quantica Education, Inc. ("Quantica," "we," "us," or "our") collects, uses, and protects your information when you use our website and learning platform (the "Service"). By using the Service, you agree to the practices described here.

1. Information We Collect

We collect only what we need to run the Service:

  • Account information. When you create an account with email and password, we collect your email address. Your password is never stored in plain text, it is hashed by Firebase Authentication before storage. When you sign in with Google, we receive your name and email address from Google.
  • Learning progress. We store your lesson completion status, XP points, Seeds, and adaptive learning state so your progress syncs across devices.
  • Payment information. Subscription payments are processed by Stripe, Inc. We never see or store your card number. We receive only a Stripe customer ID and your current subscription status (active, cancelled, etc.).
  • Site interaction data. Our analytics and advertising tools collect pages visited, clicks and taps, scroll depth, pointer movement, approximate location from your IP address, and device and browser type, and they set their own identifiers. Section 7 names each tool and says where it runs, and section 6 explains how to opt out.

2. How We Use Your Information

  • To create and manage your account
  • To save and sync your learning progress
  • To process subscription payments and grant access to paid content
  • To send account-related emails (password resets, subscription receipts)
  • To improve the course content and platform based on aggregate usage patterns
  • To measure our advertising and show Quantica ads to people who have visited the site

We do not sell your personal information for money. We do run two tools that go beyond counting visits, the Meta pixel and Microsoft Clarity. The Meta pixel tells Meta that a browser visited a page here, so we can advertise Quantica to people who have been to the site. California law counts that as sharing personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising, so we call it that here. Section 7 says what each tool does and where it runs, and section 6 says how to switch both of them off.

3. Children's Privacy (COPPA)

You have to be 13 or older to hold a Quantica account. That is a hard rule, not a formality. We do not open accounts for anyone under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from a child under 13.

The lessons are written for roughly grades 5 to 12, so plenty of learners here are younger than 13. The way that works is simple. A parent or guardian holds the account in their own name and email address, and the child sits down and learns on it. The name, email address, and billing details we hold belong to the adult. We never ask the child for a name, an email address, an address, or a photo.

Progress data, such as which lessons are finished and which problems were answered correctly, is stored against the account and we treat it as the account holder's data. We do not ask for or knowingly collect anything that identifies the child.

The confirmation box at signup is our record that the person creating the account says they are 13 or older. It is not a way to consent on behalf of a younger account holder, because we do not permit account holders under 13 at all.

Milo, our tutor, is a chat box, so anything typed into it reaches us. Please tell your learner not to type their name, school, address, or other personal details into it.

The free lesson pages a search engine can reach, the ones you can read without signing in, carry only Google Analytics. We deliberately keep the advertising and session-recording tools off those pages, because that is where a child is most likely to arrive on their own. Section 7 says exactly where each tool runs.

If we learn that an account holder is under 13, we will close the account and delete the personal information we hold for it. If you believe a child under 13 has given us personal information, write to privacy@quanticaedu.com and we will delete it promptly. Parents can also write to us at any time to see or delete the data on their account.

4. Third-Party Services

We use a small number of outside services to run the platform and to understand how it is used.

  • Firebase (Google LLC). Authentication, database storage, and web hosting. Firebase is governed by Google's privacy policies.
  • Google Analytics (Google LLC). Aggregate usage statistics, meaning page views and course progress events. Advertising features and ad personalization are disabled.
  • Stripe, Inc. Payment processing. Stripe is PCI-DSS compliant and governed by Stripe's privacy policy.
  • Meta Platforms, Inc. The Meta pixel, which tells Meta that a browser visited a page here so we can advertise Quantica and tell whether an ad worked. Section 6 explains how to turn it off.
  • Microsoft Corporation. Microsoft Clarity on our public marketing pages, which records page interactions as heatmaps and short playbacks so we can see where the site confuses people.

Apart from the services listed above, we do not share your personal information with anyone.

5. Data Retention

We keep your account and progress data for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account, we will delete the personal information in our own systems within 30 days, except where we have to keep it for legal or financial reasons. Payment records, for example, may be kept for up to 7 years for tax purposes.

That 30 day commitment covers what we hold, which is your account record, your learning progress, and your billing record. It does not cover the analytics and advertising services named in sections 4 and 7. Their copy of the data sits in their systems on their own retention schedules, which we do not set and cannot override. We can stop sending them anything new, and turning on Global Privacy Control does that for the browser you turn it on in. When you ask us to delete your data, we will pass the request on to those services wherever they give us a way to do it, and we will point you to their own deletion tools for the rest.

6. Your Rights

You can see, correct, or delete your account information at any time by contacting us. California residents have additional rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA, including the right to know what personal information we have collected, the right to have it corrected or deleted, and the right to opt out of sharing for cross-context behavioral advertising. We do not sell personal information for money. We do share information with Meta through the Meta pixel so we can advertise Quantica. California law counts that as sharing, and you can opt out of it.

Our opt-out is Global Privacy Control. If your browser sends the Global Privacy Control signal, we check for it on every page load and we do not load the Meta pixel or Microsoft Clarity on that visit. Google Analytics still runs, because we configure it with Google Signals and ad personalization turned off and we do not use it to build advertising audiences. Global Privacy Control is a recognized opt-out signal under California law. Some browsers, including Firefox, Brave, and DuckDuckGo, have the setting built in, and there are free extensions for the rest. It applies to every site you visit, not just ours.

There are two limits worth knowing about. Global Privacy Control is set per browser and per device, so a phone and a laptop each need it turned on. It also applies from the moment we see it, so it cannot pull back data that was already shared. If you would rather ask a person, email privacy@quanticaedu.com and ask us to stop sharing, and we will handle it by hand.

We do not act on Do Not Track. It is an older browser signal that was never given an agreed meaning, so we do not rely on it.

We will not charge you more, give you less, or treat you differently for opting out.

If you are located in the European Union or United Kingdom, you have rights under the GDPR, including the right to access, correct, or erase your data, and the right to data portability. We do not load the Meta pixel or Microsoft Clarity for visitors in Europe or the United Kingdom at all, because those tools need prior consent there and we do not run a consent banner. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@quanticaedu.com.

7. Cookies and Local Storage

We use browser local storage to remember your sign-in and your learning progress between visits. Three outside tools also run on our pages and set cookies or identifiers of their own. This list is all of them, and since we do not use a cookie banner, a fourth tool would go on this list before it went on the site.

  • Google Analytics 4 (Google LLC). Counts visits and course progress, so we can see which pages people read and how far learners get. We run it with Google Signals and ad personalization turned off, so it does not feed advertising profiles. This one runs on every page.
  • Meta pixel (Meta Platforms, Inc.). Tells Meta that a browser visited a page here, so we can show Quantica ads on Facebook and Instagram and tell whether they worked. It runs on our marketing pages and inside the course app, because that is the only way we can tell that an ad led to someone signing up. It reports which page was visited and which of a short list of actions happened, such as starting a subscription. It does not receive your lesson answers, your conversations with Milo, your name, or your email address. This is the advertising one, and it is the reason section 6 exists.
  • Microsoft Clarity (Microsoft Corporation). Turns page use into heatmaps and short playbacks, so we can find the parts of the site that confuse people. It runs on our public marketing pages only. It never runs inside the course app, so it never sees a lesson, an answer, or a tutor conversation.

Session recording sounds worse than it is, so here is the literal version. Clarity notes where the pointer moved, what was clicked or tapped, how far the page scrolled, and how the page was laid out, then replays that to us as a silent reconstruction of the page. It is not a video of you. There is no camera, no microphone, no recording of your screen, and nothing from your other tabs. We run Clarity with text masking on, so what you type into a form is not captured, and password and payment fields are never recorded.

The free lesson pages that search engines index carry Google Analytics and nothing else. Neither the Meta pixel nor Clarity loads there. Those pages are the ones a young learner is most likely to reach without an adult, so we keep the advertising and recording tools off them deliberately.

If your browser sends the Global Privacy Control signal, neither the Meta pixel nor Clarity loads at all and only Google Analytics runs. The same is true for visitors in Europe and the United Kingdom. Section 6 explains that opt-out in full.

8. Security

We take reasonable steps to protect your information, including using HTTPS for all data transmission and relying on Firebase's built-in security features. No system is perfectly secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security, but we take the protection of your data seriously.

9. Changes to This Policy

If we make material changes to this policy, we will notify registered users by email and post an updated version here with a new effective date. Your continued use of the Service after the effective date constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

10. Contact Us

For privacy questions, data requests, or concerns about children's data, please contact us at privacy@quanticaedu.com.
